newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks expected to hover, lack direction.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks expected to hover, lack direction.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to hover around current levels in the Wednesday session, amid a lack of strong factors to provide direction, brokers said. They said there was a strong wait-and-see attitude ahead of the March futures-and-options settlement at the end of the week.
On Tuesday, the Nikkei 225 average closed up 153.83 points, or 0.85 percent, at 18,267.72. Its March futures gained 130 points to 18,210 and its June futures rose to 18,180.

"Blue chips are showing signs of slowing down but lower-priced shares are being bought and the move should continue and provide the market with support," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities.

Brokers said media reports that Japan Telecom Co Ltd and International Telecom Japan Inc (ITJ) plan to merge later this year to compete with giant carrier Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) could ignite activity in the telecommunications sector.
"The sector, although it has the potential, has not been the focus of trade lately," a "Big Four" broker said.
"News of this sort will stimulate trading activity in the sector," he added.
Market sources expect the Nikkei average to move between 18,000 and 18,500.
